objectives: This course serves as a comprehensive introduction to environmental organic chemistry, designed to support students in understanding key principles such as chemical potential. It is structured to be accessible, even for individuals with limited backgrounds in chemistry, ensuring that foundational concepts are clearly explained. Beyond its role as an academic resource, the course also provides practical tools for assessing the hazards and risks associated with organic chemicals. By equipping learners with both theoretical knowledge and applied skills, it aims to empower environmental students to contribute meaningfully to the field of environmental protection.
content:
Introduction
Background thermodynamics and kinetics
Vapor pressure
Solubility and activity coefficient in water
Air-organic solvent or air-water partitioning (KH)
Organic liquid-water partitioning (KOW)
Sorption process and transformation reactions of organic pollutants
Ion exchange
Chemical Precipitation
Coagulation/ Flocculation
Advanced Oxidation Processes and Disinfection
Photolysis
Electrochemical method
books:
1.	Rene P. Schwarzenbach, Philip M. Gschwend, Dieter M. Imboden, Environmental Organic Chemistry, Wiley 2002
2.	Teh Fu Yen, Chemical Processes for Environmental Engineering, World Scientific Publishing Company,  2007
